findings.text: Isolation entry accepts a folio plus a staging list and reports success for non huge input, for a referenced folio that could be isolated, and for a free folio that could be dissolved and replaced. Gigantic sizes are rejected with a memory exhaustion signal to prevent retry, while other failures report busy.

Range replacement entry walks a caller supplied pfn interval and substitutes free huge folios that are not gigantic. It exits early when no candidates exist, advances by the remaining span of a compound folio or by buddy extent otherwise, returns memory exhaustion upon encountering a gigantic free folio, and propagates replacement helper failures.
Drain entry checks a global lock free free list for pending huge page frees and flushes the associated work item only when the list is non empty, otherwise returning immediately.
Boot allocation entry provides node exact placement when a valid node id is given, otherwise distributes successive requests across bootmem nodes using a rotating cursor held in the size class.

Boot structure initialization entry prepares shared vmemmap tail pages where the optimization is enabled and then converts every per node boot page list into initialized folios in parallel across node ids.

Size class boot sizing driver skips gigantic allocation when a CMA reservation exists but the early CMA path is inactive, honors explicit per node maxima when any are set, otherwise performs balanced allocation with gigantic and normal paths, and adjusts configured maxima on shortfall.

Pool counts stay stable during replacement because removal of the old folio and accounting plus enqueue of the fresh folio occur while holding the same central lock. The fresh folio enters with no references and the old folio is released only after unlock.

Gigantic huge pages never enter the dissolve or range replacement paths. They are fenced with a memory exhaustion result so callers abort rather than retry, avoiding a dependency cycle with contiguous allocation.

Early CMA is selected only for gigantic size classes when a global only mode is set and the architecture lacks its own huge boot allocator. Boot reservation first tries the requested node CMA and, unless exact placement was demanded, falls back to other bootmem nodes. Without early CMA the memblock path sized by the huge page size is used, with null fallbacks reporting absence.

Boot pages that cross zones without early CMA are queued without a zones valid marker for later reclamation, preserving the requested node for accounting. All other boot pages are queued at the tail with the marker set and their trailing pages marked as no init reserved.

The central huge page spin lock guards validation of huge state, reference count, queued freed state, size class lookup, freelist removal, new folio accounting and enqueue. Bulk boot insertion uses the interrupt saving variant per folio to shorten hold time.

The central lock is never held across fresh folio allocation, isolation attempts, scheduling yields, or release of old or spare folios. After each drop the retry loop revalidates all folio state because concurrent free or dissolve may have occurred.

Replacement follows a retry machine with outcomes for already freed, still referenced, zero referenced but not yet queued, and genuinely free. The first two discard any spare folio, the third yields and retries, and the last allocates a spare if needed then swaps the folios.

Reservation accounting uses three outcomes for reuse of an existing reservation, need for an additional reservation, and enforced new reservation. The enforced outcome behaves like needed but selects a distinct transaction completion path.

Boot conversion moves each boot page through vmemmap reservation setup, new folio setup, propagation of pre optimized and CMA markers, staging on a temporary list, bulk vmemmap processing, conditional tail completion, migratetype setup, and locked accounting with enqueue, restoring managed counts except for CMA pages.

The boot page record carries queue linkage, a pointer to its owning size class, and a flags word that distinguishes CMA origin, validated zone placement, and prior vmemmap optimization, queried by small predicate helpers.

Compound head setup records order and initializes large map count, page mapped count, machine id tracking, pin and entire map counts, and deferred list linkage, with subsets enabled by word size, order threshold, and build options.

A folio targeted for replacement may be freed or dissolved concurrently, so every access rechecks huge state under lock. A zero referenced folio that has not yet been queued is treated as transient and retried after a scheduling point rather than reported as busy.

Range replacement samples buddy order without the zone lock, so the value may be stale and cause a free huge folio to be skipped but not corrupted. Boot pages lacking zone validation are freed back to memblock with a warning and subtracted from allocation totals, and any shortfall lowers the configured maxima.
MAP_CHG_REUSE and MAP_CHG_NEEDED and MAP_CHG_ENFORCED correspond respectively to zero and one and two.

Boot folio lists undergo bulk vmemmap optimization before per folio handling, with a no operation fallback when the feature is disabled. Folios not marked optimized receive full tail initialization starting after the reserved prefix, while already optimized folios skip that step.

Boot allocation uses multithreaded helpers for per node conversion and for pool filling. Worker count defaults to one quarter of online processors with a minimum of one, and allocation retries only when vmemmap optimization could have reclaimed memory and the prior pass made progress.

Total CMA reservation size reports the configured global size when the feature is present and zero otherwise. When a reservation exists but early CMA is inactive, gigantic boot allocation is skipped with a one time warning.
CMA boot reservation returns immediately on success or when exact node placement was requested, otherwise probes remaining bootmem nodes once each and reports null when no reservation succeeds.
Boot folio migratetype is initialized per pageblock, using CMA initialization for CMA folios and movable initialization otherwise, with an alignment check on the head pfn.
